chip_grid_axes_note: the two ground axes of a burst are perpendicular: the range axis is reported as a line (mod 180 deg), the azimuth axis is that line rotated by 90 deg, and which of the two perpendicular senses is the flight direction follows from the orbit direction reported per chip in haltern_bursts.json

event_corroboration.note: the collapse date of this record is read off the map's own edit history: the version named here added damage:date=2021-09-29 within a day of the event, from a public changeset

note: this anchor supports a statement about *which structure stood here and when it collapsed*, not a band/edge layer: such a layer needs a resolvable ground extent per pixel along the band axis, and ``structure_vs_pixel_grid`` is the number that says how far this record is from that
site: Haltern AV9 Wind Park (Kreis Recklinghausen, NRW)
status: anchor reference - no edge layer is claimed: a 7x7 window per acquisition, no rect/pixel-spacing spec and no per-section coordinates (see code/haltern/README.md)

structure.source: base = the committed structure.width_m of the onboarded asset; rotor = the 149 m swept diameter of the model tag of the OSM node (N149)

structure_vs_window.note: the structure lies outside the frame: the tower base alone is 2.4-2.6 px across range and 0.6-0.6 px across azimuth, while a 7x7 frame reaches 6 px at most (3 px from its centre) - so not one committed pixel spans the base, the base is contained on no orbit, and there is nothing to run a band test on. Containment needs 5-5 px per side (13-13 px with Bautzen's +/-4-row ROI): a frame of 5 px per side is 25 samples (0.5x the committed 49 px) and 13 px per side 169 (3.4x) - the cost is quadratic in the side. The N149 rotor, 149 m = 39.6-43.4 px across range, *would* span such a frame - but a rotor is not a band/edge object: its ground projection is a line whose length and direction are set by the yaw, which neither the export nor the catalogue carries. That is the second half of blocker 4 of code/haltern/README.md: containment is purchasable with a wider window, a *testable* edge is not.

turbine.anchor: the node itself - the turbine's own OSM object, never an area/polygon (the Bergsoysund analysis measured a -81..+7 m shape error, rms 56 m, for a polygon anchor)

window.note: one 7x7 complex window per acquisition at the asset point; the export committed no per-section coordinates (its segment_latitude / segment_longitude columns are empty for all five mast sections), so this package has no second anchor and no rect spec
